summary:
## Verdict

I'd recommend **not merging** until this branch is rebased onto current `main` and re-done as a true delta — head `SKILL.md` is a **stale v1.6.2 / four-capability** snapshot that would regress the shipped parent skill contract on `main` (`2.5.1`, five capabilities including `apply-review`).

## Narrative

The PR description frames this as a light narrative reframe of today's skill ("Local Companion" → "Local & CI Companion", 522 → 511 lines, Steps 0–5 byte-identical to `main`). That does **not** match the tree this PR would land against:

| Surface | `main` (base `38c6144…`) | This branch (head) |
|---|---|---|
| Frontmatter `version` | `2.5.1` | `1.6.2` |
| Capabilities | **Five**, incl. [`apply-review`](skills/ai-diff-reviewer/apply-review/SKILL.md) | **Four** — `apply-review` absent from router + worktree |
| Pin examples | `@v2.1.0` / `uses: …@v2` | `@v1.4.2` / (stale) `@v1` in the workflow sample on this tip |
| Parity text | methodology + severity; IAR may shorten CI round 2+ | "identical reviews" |
| Extra sections on `main` | CI-only surfaces (IAR, `skip-review-label`, incremental/usage), apply-review activation + disambiguation, check-status vs recommendation | missing |

Importantly, **current `main` already has** the H1 "Local & CI Companion Skill", the "Two audiences, same skill" frame, the Surface column, flows-before-install ordering, and the "Default flow" header. The interesting editorial work in this PR is largely already on `main` (and `main` went further). The three-dot diff looks small only because the branch forked from a **pre-`apply-review` / pre-v2** ancestor; it is not a safe patch on today's file.

If this tip were taken as the resolution of a merge conflict on `skills/ai-diff-reviewer/SKILL.md`, consumers' coding agents would stop routing "what did CI say?" / "apply the review" to `apply-review`, get wrong major pins, and lose the IAR parity caveats. That is a public skill-contract break, not a docs nit.

**What to do instead**
